modules.name: road_mac_probe
modules.description: Single-inflight signed INT8 8-input by 3-output MAC arithmetic probe with explicit INT32 overflow faulting.

ports.name: i_rstn
ports.description: Asynchronous active-low reset that cancels in-flight work.

ports.name: i_input_valid
ports.description: Holds the complete input payload valid until accepted.

ports.name: i_first
ports.description: Selects the bias payload instead of the retained accumulator.

ports.name: i_last
ports.description: Requests publication after this accepted beat.

ports.name: i_lane_mask
ports.description: Enables each activation lane for all three outputs.

ports.name: i_activation_data
ports.description: Eight signed INT8 activations with lane zero in the least-significant byte.

ports.name: i_weight_data
ports.description: Three consecutive groups of eight signed INT8 weights.

ports.name: i_bias_data
ports.description: Three signed INT32 biases with output zero in the least-significant word.

ports.name: i_result_ready
ports.description: Accepts the held normal result or fault terminal.

ports.name: o_input_ready
ports.description: Allows one new beat when no earlier beat remains in flight.

ports.name: o_result_valid
ports.description: Qualifies a held result or fault terminal until ready is asserted.

ports.name: o_result_data
ports.description: Three signed INT32 accumulator results, forced to zero when fault is high.

ports.name: o_fault
ports.description: Marks any channel candidate outside the signed INT32 range.

reset.name: i_rstn
reset.values: All valid, fault, accumulator, and pipeline registers clear to zero.

behavior: An input transfers only when i_input_valid and o_input_ready are high on a rising edge.
Each enabled lane computes three signed INT8 products, giving 24 registered products per accepted beat.
Registered pair, quad, and dot stages reduce each group of eight products without truncation.
A first beat adds each dot product to its matching bias; a continuation beat adds to the retained accumulator.
A non-last normal beat commits the three candidates without asserting o_result_valid.
A last normal beat commits and publishes the three candidates.
Any signed INT32 overflow suppresses commit, publishes o_fault with zero result data, and cannot be interpreted as success.
While o_result_valid is high and i_result_ready is low, result data and fault remain unchanged.
A terminal beat raises o_result_valid nine rising-edge intervals after its input acceptance.
constraints: The implementation accepts at most one beat in flight and does not claim full-layer throughput.

The accepted-beat interval is eleven cycles after a normal continuation beat, and thirteen cycles after an immediately accepted terminal; each output stall cycle extends the terminal interval one-for-one.
The 24 registered multipliers describe spatial arithmetic only; this probe does not accept 24 products per cycle.
Each combinational source cone and real-operation budget remains at or below three.
The arithmetic probe contains no ROM, DDR, requantization, activation LUT, or production top-level connection.
corner_cases: A zero mask adds no products but still obeys first and last semantics.
INT8 -128 times -128 produces positive 16384 and is retained without narrowing.
Bias is selected only for an accepted first beat.
Positive or negative signed INT32 overflow publishes fault and leaves the retained accumulator unchanged.
Reset during any pipeline stage cancels the transaction without a late result.
Input payload must remain stable while valid is high and ready is low.
verification_cases: Python unittest covers 1024 fixed-seed random single-beat cases plus negative extrema, masks, multi-beat accumulation, stalls, reset, and overflow.
The Verilog testbench consumes Python-generated vectors and compares every normal terminal exactly.
At fixed cycles after each acceptance, the Verilog testbench compares all 24 products, 12 pair sums, 6 quad sums, and 3 dot sums against Python-generated banks.
The Verilog testbench requires the terminal valid indication exactly nine cycles after input acceptance.
The Verilog testbench holds output ready low for three cycles and checks stable valid, data, and fault.
The Verilog testbench asserts reset during reduction and checks that no terminal survives.

timing_diagrams.title: Two-beat accumulation with held result
timing_diagrams.description: The first non-last beat commits internally. The continuation last beat later publishes one result, which remains stable until result ready is asserted.
